The current extension treats every workspace root as a Python project, regardless of its contents, as documented in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/blob/main/docs/managing-python-projects.md. Workspace roots also cannot currently be removed through the Remove Python Project action. This leaves a product question for mixed-language workspaces: should every root remain an environment-association container, or should non-Python roots be excluded or removable? Keeping this open to settle that behavior and make the documentation consistent.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report and for confirming the workaround. Command-based activation is intentionally the default because it can activate environments in any shell; `shellStartup` is the non-disruptive opt-in for supported shells, and `off` is available where no automatic activation is wanted. The same Ctrl+C behavior was subsequently reviewed and closed as designed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/issues/1570. Please continue using `"python-envs.terminal.autoActivationType": "shellStartup"` for this workflow.

rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the detailed Snakemake context. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/issues/1671, which tracks Conda environments appearing in Environment Manager but not in Python: Select Interpreter or Jupyter's Python-environment kernel picker, so we can consolidate there. This report adds useful evidence: the environments are discovered through `.snakemake/conda/**`, have hashed names and `ipykernel` installed, and become available only after manually entering their interpreter paths. A related compatibility-adapter fix has also landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/pull/26112.
rows.verifyEvidence: A asks how to surface Snakemake's hash-named .snakemake/conda envs via workspaceSearchPaths (discovery of non-registered envs); B's named conda envs ARE discovered but fail to render in the picker UI — different mechanisms.

rows.proposedComment:
Thanks for the detailed reproduction and syscall data. The configure retry
behavior belongs in the environment area here, while the unbounded glob expansion and
malformed-input loop appear to require corresponding work in

terminal.launchArgs not being used
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. This was fixed by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python/commit/3df36ecb26e4b3c3d3bed982c34e5d1a2498f3b9 and shipped in Python extension 2025.14.0. The run-file integration now reads `python.terminal.launchArgs` and passes those arguments through the Python Environments terminal API, so this can be closed as resolved.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff reads pythonSettings.terminal.launchArgs and prepends them to the run-file terminal args, which previously passed only the file path — exactly the reported omission when running a Python script.

SimpleDebounce should be a disposable
rows.proposedComment: Thanks for the report. The requested disposable implementation was added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/commit/7d528717437752e7e5dc00481e1725ccb3e97ee7 through https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-python-environments/pull/952 and shipped in v1.12.0. `SimpleDebounce` now extends `Disposable`, and `dispose()` clears any pending timeout, so this is resolved.
rows.verifyEvidence: The diff makes SimpleDebounce extend Disposable and adds the exact requested dispose() clearing the pending timeout, so a disposed debouncer no longer fires.
